questions.question_text: Insanity sometimes is the sane response to an insane society. This was proposed by
questions.explanation: RD Laing was a prominent anti­psychiatrist who wrote 'The Divided Self'.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT true concerning research ethics?

options.text: Subjects can be recruited by contacting medical colleagues
Written approval must be obtained from ethics committees
Financial incentives can be offered for subjects to participate in research
Advertisements can be used to recruit subjects
A subject is ethically bound to complete a study after giving written informed consent

correct_answer.text: A subject is ethically bound to complete a study after giving written informed consent

correct_answers.text: A subject is ethically bound to complete a study after giving written informed consent

questions.explanation: Signing a consent form does not mean that they cannot discontinue the study during its course.

questions.question_text: What is the number of women that have been reported being amputated in the genital area?
questions.explanation: WHO has estimated that 100 to 140 million girls and women worldwide are currently living with the consequences of FGM.

questions.question_text: In prematurely born infants, after which week of pregnancy are we legally able to resuscitate an infant irrespective of parental wishes?
questions.explanation: In United Kingdom women have access to termination of pregnancy for maternal reasons until 24 weeks completed gestation; so it is rational children born at or beyond 25 weeks gestation are treated according to the child's perceived best interests even if this is not in accordance with parental wishes.

questions.question_text: In clinical psychiatric population which of the following disorders is more common in higher social classes?
questions.explanation: For a long time now it is debated whether the social class differences in anorexia reflects help seeking or referral patterns only or the actual disease prevalence.

questions.question_text: Partial adaptation of a new culture without giving up one's culture of origin completely is called
questions.explanation: Assimilation refers to the partial adaptation of a new culture (seen in immigrants or refugees) without giving up one's culture of origin completely.

questions.question_text: The term refrigerator mother is associated with which of the following mental illness?
questions.explanation: Mothers with autistic children were blamed to be 'refrigerator mothers' who 'defrosted just enough to produce a baby' but remained emotionally cold, inflexible and lacking warmth in the parental relationship.

questions.question_text: Institutional neurosis was described by
questions.explanation: Russell Barton (1976) described 'institutional neurosis', characterized by symptoms such as apathy, lack of initiative, loss of interest and submissiveness.

questions.question_text: The four prima facie ethical principles were promulgated by
questions.explanation: The prima facie principles were promulgated by Beauchamp and Childress.

questions.question_text: Which of the following risk factor is likely to be causative in a young man diagnosed with schizophrenia?

options.text: Having lost his mother before the age of 14

questions.explanation: Immigration is one of the strongest known risk factors for schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which class of psychotropic medication are the most likely ones to impair driving performance?
questions.explanation: All drugs acting on the central nervous system can impair alertness, concentration and driving performance. This is particularly so at the initiation of treatment or soon after and when the dosage is being increased.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is classified under higher-level principle?
questions.explanation: Higher level principles include Deontology (Rights and duties or Rules) and Teleology (practice based on best interests / outcomes).

questions.question_text: When a psychiatric patient is unwell, family and friends report their actions to mental health professionals in an attempt to get them admitted to an institution. What was the term used by Goffman to describe it?
questions.explanation: Goffman also described the social/moral career of a mental patient. i.e., the process whereby a person with social ties, friends, and family in the community is institutionalized and converted into an inmate whose world is limited to his immediate hospital ambience.

questions.question_text: An Asian immigrant in England is observed to practice his religion and cultural traditions at home but adapts well especially at work with a good degree of fluency in both English and his native language. This type of enculturation is called
questions.explanation: Biculturalism appears to be more adaptive and associated with minimal acculturation stress.

questions.question_text: In which of the following disorder an overrepresentation of higher social class is seen in brothers and children of the patients?
questions.explanation: An overrepresentation is found in the higher occupational class in bipolar probands' brothers and children.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a semi-structured interview that can be used to gather information regarding expressed emotions from family members of a patient with psychosis?
questions.explanation: Camberwell Family Interview is a semi-structured interview carried out with relatives of patients with Schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Torts are wrongs for which a person is liable in
questions.explanation: Torts are errors for which a person is liable in civil as opposed to criminal law.

questions.question_text: Major recurring themes behind the stigma against mental illness includes all except
questions.explanation: Hayward and Bright described four major recurring themes or beliefs behind the stigma against mental illness.

questions.question_text: Melting pot model refers to which of the following types of countries?

options.text: Countries with high population attrition due to emigration

questions.explanation: The United States is often quoted as a Melting Pot of various immigrant societies.

questions.question_text: A 12-year-old girl is called by names at her school after her dad's admission at the local psychiatric hospital. This is called
questions.explanation: Courtesy stigma refers to the stigmatization an unaffected person experiences due to his or her relationship with a person who bears a stigma.

questions.question_text: A boy whose mother has depression has a high likelihood to develop one of the following conditions before age 20?
questions.explanation: The strongest risk factor for depression is a personal or family history of depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following increases the likelihood that a patient with a particular disease gets stigmatized?

options.text: Disease is thought to be inflicted by an external agent
Disease leads to disruption in social interactions
Disease elicits pity but no disgust in others

correct_answer.text: Disease leads to disruption in social interactions

correct_answers.text: Disease leads to disruption in social interactions

questions.explanation: The degree of stigmatisation is directly proportional to the degree of disruption in social interaction produced by the condition.

questions.question_text: According to Holmes and Rahe social readjustment scale, which of the following has the highest life change value?
questions.explanation: Divorce tops the rest of the stressors list and generates about 73 units.

questions.question_text: A patient refuses to have a nasogastric intubation after an overdose, and the AandE consultant feels this procedure is potentially lifesaving and complies with expected standard of care. The best course of action is

options.text: Assume that the patient does not have the capacity to decide whether to have the procedure or not
Refer the patient to a psychiatrist
Do not perform the procedure if the patient is determined to have the capacity to make this decision
Sedate the patient first and then carry out the procedure
Try repeatedly and convince the patient that the procedure is necessary until they eventually consent

correct_answer.text: Do not perform the procedure if the patient is determined to have the capacity to make this decision

correct_answers.text: Do not perform the procedure if the patient is determined to have the capacity to make this decision

questions.explanation: Patients have the right to refuse medical care, even when it seems medically necessary to save their life.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is regarded as 'Father of Sociology'?
questions.explanation: Emile Durkheim, a French journalist, formally established the study of sociology.

questions.question_text: One year after losing her job of 15 years, a depressed woman gets another job but unfortunately within two weeks she loses the new job. She feels 'stuck in her life'. Which of the following category does this event belong?
questions.explanation: Entrapment includes long-term sustained entrapment includes serious difficulties that can only get worse or persist according to the subject; or a failed positive event where a potential fresh start went disastrously wrong within 1-2 wk, leaving the person stuck in square one.

questions.question_text: A West African student presents with lethargy, insomnia, palpitation and anxiety. Choose one culture-bound syndrome:
questions.explanation: The 'brain fag' syndrome, which was first reported from West Africa in 1960 among students, has been shown to occur very widely in African students in western educational systems south of the Sahara.

questions.question_text: A patient admitted at an inpatient unit is making steady progress. But his symptoms worsen whenever he comes back from home leave. His mother criticises him of being very reluctant and lazy to get involved in 'normal life'. The next step in management must consider
questions.explanation: Classical studies by Brown et al., and Vaughn and Leff indicated four times higher relapse rates for patients with schizophrenia who were discharged to parents who were hostile, critical, or overly involved.

questions.question_text: The concept of schizophrenogenic-mother was proposed by
questions.explanation: The concept of schizophrenogenic-mother was coined by Freida Fromm-Reichmann.

questions.question_text: The term total institution is associated with
questions.explanation: A total institution is a place of work and residence where a great number of similarly situated people, cut off from the wider community for a considerable time, together lead an enclosed, formally administered round of life. The term was coined and defined by American sociologist Erving Goffman.

questions.question_text: Which of the following aspects best describes one's ethnicity?
questions.explanation: Ethnicity is perceived as partially changeable entity determined by social pressure and psychological need characterized by a sense of group identity and belonging.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a vulnerability factor for depression in Brown and Harris study?

options.text: Having 3 or more children under 15 living at home
Absence of a close confiding relationship
Loss of mother before age of 11
Having a long standing physical illness

correct_answer.text: Having a long standing physical illness

correct_answers.text: Having a long standing physical illness

questions.explanation: Social and economic circumstances associated with the onset of depression in women living in inner urban London were studied by Brown and Harris in 1978.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes the code of ethical recommendations used currently to guide clinical research worldwide?
questions.explanation: Helsinki declaration contains the current research ethics code in practice.

questions.question_text: A depressed 55-year-old man reports a high amount of adverse life events, but no positive events preceding his first episode of depression. Which of the following explanation is NOT correct?

options.text: Stressful life events have established association with depressive disorder
He is recalling more stressful life events due to cognitive bias
His depression is probably due to absence of positive life events
Recurrent episodes have less preceding life events than the first episode
Social adversity experienced from an event depends on contextual rating by the patient

correct_answer.text: His depression is probably due to absence of positive life events

correct_answers.text: His depression is probably due to absence of positive life events

questions.explanation: It is shown that the frequency of desirable (or entrance life events) was comparable in controls and the depressed population.

questions.question_text: Which of the following type of life events predicts the onset of pure depressive illness?
questions.explanation: Humiliation events induce defeat and submission responses that may be directly related to depression.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man has chest pain and dizziness but his blood tests and ECG are normal. He is advised to take medications, fat-restricted diet, exercise. This is called
questions.explanation: The concept of illness behaviour was largely defined and adopted during the second half of the twentieth century.

questions.question_text: Best evidence base to decrease alcohol harm is

options.text: Education of public about harm of alcohol

questions.explanation: When other factors are held constant, such as income and the price of other goods, a rise in alcohol prices leads to less alcohol consumption and vice versa.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about Camberwell family interview is not true?

options.text: It is carried out with patient
It is a semi-structured standard interview
The rating is based on content and vocal tone

correct_answer.text: It is carried out with patient

correct_answers.text: It is carried out with patient

questions.explanation: Camberwell Family Interview is a semi-structured interview carried out with relatives of patients with Schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true with regards to Changing Minds campaign?

options.text: It is focussed on geriatric mental health issues
It provides a legal clause against stigma
It is not a part of Care Programme Approach
It is an ongoing programme against stigma
It is an initiative from World Health Organisation

correct_answer.text: It is not a part of Care Programme Approach

correct_answers.text: It is not a part of Care Programme Approach

questions.explanation: Concern about the stigma of mental illness culminated in the Royal College of Psychiatrists' 5-year 'Changing Minds' campaign.

questions.question_text: The following are true in relation to the biopsychosocial model except

options.text: It is based on the fact that each system is at the same time a component of higher system
It is similar to biomedical model
It was proposed by George Engel
It is based on systems theory
The hierarchy and continuum of natural systems were discussed to explain biopsychosocial model

correct_answer.text: It is similar to biomedical model

correct_answers.text: It is similar to biomedical model

questions.explanation: The biopsychosocial model is a systems theory­based explanation of disease models.

questions.question_text: The phenomenon of relative deprivation is explained by
questions.explanation: A scoring system developed by the British general practitioner Brian Jarman for the level of social deprivation in a community.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes an extreme anxiety symptom where a person thinks that his penis is shrinking into his abdomen, and he may die as a result?
questions.explanation: Koro is known as genital retraction syndrome. Patients believe that their genitals will be completely sucked into the body, causing death.

questions.question_text: Understanding the impact of a life event in light of one's current social context and self-perspective is called contextual rating of social adversity. Which of the following employs the above method?

options.text: Holmes and Rahe social adjustment scale

questions.explanation: Brown and Harris popularized a different method whereby life events are graded according to the inherent meaning of the events to the individual concerned.

questions.question_text: Which of the following ethical principles is not associated with Charaka?
questions.explanation: Charaka promoted 4 Cs - confidentiality, caring practice, continuous professional development and compassion.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man received inpatient detoxification two weeks ago and since then has been staying away from alcohol use. According to Prochaska's model, which stage is he in?
questions.explanation: The maintenance stage is the phase wherein the person strives to maintain gains made.

questions.question_text: A clinician refuses to prescribe clozapine to an elderly lady with resistant schizophrenia as she had developed neutropenia 13 years ago when it was first prescribed to her. Which of the following ethical principle is maintained here?
questions.explanation: Non-maleficence refers to avoiding harm (primum non nocere).

questions.question_text: Which of the following syndromes refer to the fear of cold seen in Chinese men?
questions.explanation: Pa-Leng is a form of frigophobia seen in China.

questions.question_text: A doctor carries out what is best for the patient, regardless of patient's own wishes. This approach can be termed as
questions.explanation: Paternalism is the interference with people's liberties or autonomy with an argument that this is done 'for their own good.'

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about abuse of children?

options.text: People who were subjected to physical abuse in childhood are more likely to abuse their own children
Abuse is inversely proportional to family size
Girls are more likely to be the subject of physical abuse and are at a greater risk of physical injury
Children with disabilities were less likely to be maltreated than children without disabilities
Boys are more likely to be the subject of sexual abuse

correct_answer.text: People who were subjected to physical abuse in childhood are more likely to abuse their own children

correct_answers.text: People who were subjected to physical abuse in childhood are more likely to abuse their own children

questions.explanation: About one­third of all individuals who were maltreated would subject their children to maltreatment.

questions.question_text: A 31-year-old woman of Inuit origin started becoming too excited for no apparent reason, taking her clothes off and throwing her naked body into cold icy water. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Piblokto is characterized by a dissociative episode with excitement often followed by seizures and coma lasting up to 12 hours.

questions.question_text: A man doesn't think drinking alcohol is a problem and doesn't want to quit. According to Prochaska's model, which stage is he in?
questions.explanation: In pre­contemplation stage, the user does not recognize that problem use exists, although this may be increasingly obvious to those around them.

questions.question_text: The notion that there are inherent distinctions among ethnic groups and that some ethnicities are biologically superior to others can be described as
questions.explanation: Racism refers to attitudes, beliefs, or behaviors that favor one group over another.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man with schizophrenia is treatment resistant. He lives with his family who apparently has high EE. Which of the following statements about EE is true?

options.text: High EE may be the cause for his schizophrenia
High EE can cause poor insight
EE can be measured using Camberwell Assessment of Needs (CANE)
High EE has no effect on relapse rates in female patients
Reducing the duration of face to face time spent with family may reduce the relapse

correct_answer.text: Reducing the duration of face to face time spent with family may reduce the relapse

correct_answers.text: Reducing the duration of face to face time spent with family may reduce the relapse

questions.explanation: In the majority of the studies, high expressed emotion was predictive of relapse in symptoms of schizophrenia nine months later for both genders.

questions.question_text: A medical student is undertaking a clinical research project and is keen to know the ethical principles that are widely implemented in medical practice. Choose the correct option:

options.text: Duty of care and good will
Respect for autonomy, beneficence and justice
Respect for autonomy, justice and confidentiality

correct_answer.text: Respect for autonomy, beneficence and justice

correct_answers.text: Respect for autonomy, beneficence and justice

questions.explanation: The four principles are the main guiding aspects of current medical practice.

questions.question_text: In UK which of the following disorders are most stigmatized?
questions.explanation: Schizophrenia and addictions were regarded most negatively in a survey measuring subjective perception of mental disorders.

questions.question_text: Before being diagnosed as having schizophrenia, Mark was regarded as a suspicious young man by his colleagues. After an acute admission, his colleagues avoided him and so he became more suspicious if anyone ever approached him. Which of the following aspect of social labeling applies to Mark's suspiciousness following diagnostic labeling?
questions.explanation: Secondary deviance is any action that takes place after primary deviance as a reaction to the institutions and the labeling.

questions.question_text: Which of the following genetic changes have been shown to influence an individual's response to stressful life events in terms of later depression?
questions.explanation: Caspi demonstrated a link between 5HT polymorphisms and life events in depressive response.

questions.question_text: Immigrants carry a higher risk of schizophrenia than the native population in UK. Which of the following is correct in this regard?

options.text: Excess risk is specific for African and Caribbean immigrants
Incidence rates of schizophrenia in Caribbean countries are higher than UK
Psychiatric hospital admission rates are lesser among ethnic minorities
Pre-psychotic segregation explains the higher risk
Significant social disadvantage in the immigrants may explain the association

correct_answer.text: Significant social disadvantage in the immigrants may explain the association

correct_answers.text: Significant social disadvantage in the immigrants may explain the association

questions.explanation: Though the frequency of most mental illnesses are found to be higher in migrants, schizophrenia has been studied the most.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a measure of expressed emotions?
questions.explanation: Five measures are considered for expressed emotions, including positive regard and emotional warmth.

questions.question_text: A doctor wants to establish a long-term therapeutic relationship with her patient. Focusing on which of the following provides the best likelihood for achieving this?

options.text: Strengths and interests of the patient

correct_answer.text: Strengths and interests of the patient

correct_answers.text: Strengths and interests of the patient

questions.explanation: The establishment of long-term therapeutic relationship hinges on understanding the strengths and interests of a patient.

questions.question_text: A patient with acute relapse of schizophrenia was given time off the ward. He came back next day with his mother who was blaming him for his illness, and 'what he has put himself through'. Which of the following actions is likely to be most helpful?

options.text: Use Mental Health Act to detain the patient to the ward
Provide psychodynamic support to the mother
Suggest Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for schizophrenia

questions.explanation: High EE can be reduced by family therapy focussed on addressing communication patterns within the family unit.

questions.question_text: A Chinese man is afraid of going out of his house. He believes that the cold wind will destroy his soul. What is the cultural bound syndrome described here?
questions.explanation: Susto (also called espanto) is known as a 'fright sickness' and can involve the belief that one's soul has been separated from the body.

questions.question_text: The 'Myth of Mental Illness' was written by
questions.explanation: Thomas Szasz wrote 'The Myth of Mental Illness' in 1961.

questions.question_text: A Japanese man is afraid of going out with his friends as he is embarrassed about his bad body odour. Despite repeated reassurances that he does not smell badly, he insists on being left alone. The most likely diagnosis is
questions.explanation: Taijin refers to a fear of losing good will of others due to imagined shortcomings of oneself.

questions.question_text: Mr. Brown is not feeling well and calls off sick at work. Which of the following behaviours, if expressed by Mr.Brown under these circumstances would be regarded as abnormal?

options.text: Seeking help from an internet doctor
Complying with treatment as prescribed by the doctor
Not carrying out normal social roles
Extending absence from work when the illness continues

questions.explanation: Taking self-blame for the illness is inconsistent with the sick role concept.

questions.question_text: A young male doctor from India gets married and moves to the UK with his wife and his two kids. The children are attending a primary school. His retired parents also join him soon after. Which of the following is true? (October 2008)

options.text: The grandparents will have the maximum difficulty in adjusting to change
The young couple will have the maximum difficulty in adjusting to change
The children will have the maximum difficulty in adjusting to change
No one can adjust to the change for next 5 years
Everyone will adjusts with same degree of ease

correct_answer.text: The grandparents will have the maximum difficulty in adjusting to change

correct_answers.text: The grandparents will have the maximum difficulty in adjusting to change

questions.explanation: The elderly find it more challenging to acculturate when compared to the younger immigrants.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is least likely to be consistent with an individual assuming the Sick Role?

options.text: The individual is relieved of his social and vocational responsibilities
The individual wants to get better
The individual takes time off work to aid recovery
The individual refuses medical help and does not accept his/her diagnosis
The individual is considered not responsible for his/her sickness

correct_answer.text: The individual refuses medical help and does not accept his/her diagnosis

correct_answers.text: The individual refuses medical help and does not accept his/her diagnosis

questions.explanation: Refusing medical help and not accepting a diagnosis is inconsistent with the sick role.

questions.question_text: A 20 years old immigrant Jamaican man develops schizophrenia. Which of the following is most likely to be true?

options.text: He is likely to be poorly educated compared to native patients
He is likely to seek professional help early in the course of his illness
His parents are likely to be from a lower socioeconomic class compared to parents of native patients
The risk of schizophrenia in his parents is likely to be similar to the risk in the parents of native patients
His immigration is likely to be due to psychotic experiences

correct_answer.text: The risk of schizophrenia in his parents is likely to be similar to the risk in the parents of native patients

correct_answers.text: The risk of schizophrenia in his parents is likely to be similar to the risk in the parents of native patients

questions.explanation: The most acceptable notion at present is that this risk is mediated by social adversity faced by immigrants.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false with respect to Nuremburg code?

options.text: The code pertains to human research ethics
Nuremburg is a place in Germany
Voluntary consent was upheld as a vital aspect of research
It is related to World War 2
Tried Japanese doctors for unfair treatment of patients

correct_answer.text: Tried Japanese doctors for unfair treatment of patients

correct_answers.text: Tried Japanese doctors for unfair treatment of patients

questions.explanation: Nuremburg code is related to the trial received by Nazi doctors after WWII.

questions.question_text: The right action is the one that has the best foreseeable consequences. This is called;
questions.explanation: Consequentialist moral theories are teleological: they aim at some goal state and evaluate the morality of actions in terms of progress toward that state.

questions.question_text: A patient with paranoid schizophrenia was enraged at a shop and killed the shopkeeper. A forensic psychiatrist who examined him feels that he needs psychiatric treatment. The court decides that he must be sentenced to prison. Which of the following ethical principle is closely related to the above scenario?
questions.explanation: The strengths of utilitarianism lie in its practicality and clarity, and legislative responsibilities of psychiatrists in public safety.

questions.question_text: According to Nuremburg code formulated after the Second World War, human experimentation can be carried out only if which of the following conditions is satisfied?

options.text: Written consent is given for infliction of more than necessary pain
A study causing harm can be completed only if carers agree with patients
Subjects are well compensated for any suffering underwent

questions.explanation: According to Nuremburg Code voluntary consent is a fundamental requirement for human experimentation.

questions.question_text: Identify the study that is related to deliberately infected individuals with hepatitis.
questions.explanation: From 1963 through 1966, studies were carried out at the Willowbrook State School where children were deliberately infected with the hepatitis virus.
